title: Great Product, Poor Cost to Maintain
body: I'm going to keep this short and simple. I bought this product because I saw this ad on TV perfectly timed with a fly buzzing past my screen. This product is AMAZING and super simple. I pulled the plastic tape off of the trap, plugged the device in and waited a few days. It caught a lot of bugs already, and I guarantee it will catch more soon. Why am I giving this 3 stars though? The cost to get new sticky traps. Doing the math, it costs close to $10 per trap refill.. Maybe I am just cheap, but that is very expensive for something that I see needing to be replaced somewhat frequently to keep its effectiveness up. I love the product but I believe for most people the cost would not be worth it at all, and it very much lowers my hopes for it. ps. it is pretty much the same price to purchase the device again, with the 3 additional traps.

And despite what I considered a high price tag for a disposable-cartridge type product I went for it. Because we have a ton of flies (it's fall and I live in a rural area.) About a week after this has been in my kitchen, I also put up a traditional strip of flypaper which now has a dozen flies on it. Still no houseflies in the zevo. I'm on the verge of saying one star, but I'll give it two because it does catch a bunch of fruit flies that I didn't know we're so bad.

title: I wouldn’t purchase again
body: I’ve seen ads for this product for a while so it immediately came to mind as a solution when we started having a fruit fly problem. I like the concept of this product but felt it wasn’t as effective as it should have been. I placed it where I had seen most of the fruit flies hanging out and it did catch a few, but I was a little disappointed that it wasn’t making much of a dent in the population. Something else I should have considered before purchasing was how brightly the blue light shines from this device. We avoid blue light around bedtime and dim the lights in our house in the evenings as we get ready to sleep and so this didn’t fit with my personal sleep hygiene preferences - but that’s honestly my fault for not thinking through how this product works before purchasing it. After giving Zevo a chance for a few days I decided to try the old apple cider vinegar in a jar with tiny holes poked in the lid method. The apple cider jar was the clear winner and captured at least 3-4 times more in a single night than the Zivo had in days. The homemade method was much cheaper too. If I could go back and do it all over again I would just do the jar trick and save money by not purchasing this product.

title: Doesn't work or is too slow.
body: Look, the idea of trying to get rid of those annoying fruit flies makes my skin crawl and my blood boil at the same time. I hate them. Most insect such as those I despise. But nothing I hate more than fruit flies. This product took AGES to catch even a couple of them, let alone the thousands that are made per day sometimes. If any of you reading this have had them, you know what I mean. They are obnoxious. Here is the thing: the quicker you kill them off, the better. This will not do it, not even close. Left them on for a month and when I went to just toss them in the garbage, I could literally count the fruit flies and other things that somehow found there way behind this to get stuck. Here is how you get rid of fruit flies MUCH QUICKER and for WAY LESS MONEY: Apple cider vinegar + ramekin or other small/medium container + clear plastic wrap + toothpick. Fill half of the ramekin with the vinegar, stretch film over the top. Poke little holes in the saran wrap. Place near infected area. After a day or two, you will be unable to count how many of those little ******* are dead in there. Rinse and repeat when it starts to get too full. I have probably killed millions with this little death pit. These are a gimmick, stay away. Especially for fruit flies. Not sure how well they work for mosquitos.

title: Not very effective for fruit flies
body: I recently went out of town for a week and left the wife on her own. We already had a couple fruit flies when I left (maybe 3-5 that I noticed), but this isn't unusual since we always buy fruit as it comes into season and this brings fruit fly eggs into the house. Before I left I just reminded her that the trap needed to be setup and she said it wouldn't be a problem. By trap, I mean the apple shaped trap you can get at just about any store where you put a little vinegar and dish soap in and it just "makes the problem go away." I have used those traps for years and they work great, I just put one on the table near the fruit bowl and one near the kitchen sink. Well, I get home and it seems the wife stopped doing dishes and taking out the trash for a week and and fruit flies had gone ham in the sink. Absolute infestation. Swarms plume from the sink when you approach it. The little apples couldn't keep up. So I figured I would try something new. The new UV trap has been setup for 4 days/3 nights. The trap is plugged in right next to the kitchen sink and all the lights are off at night so this trap has had the best chance of succeeding. It has caught, a disappointing number of flies. Maybe 15-20 in that number of days when the number in the house is multiple hundred. I actually just before writing this unplugged it and waved it around over the sink and caught 4 time more in 30 seconds waving this thing around than I have in 4 days. This is probably fine as a very minor preventative, but it costs way more than the little apples, is far more noticeable and not any more effective. I do not recommend.

title: These are worthless. Do not buy them.
body: DO NOT waste your money on this product. I have had two of these since September. The picture is after 6 months. There is nothing but cat hair. I always have an issue when I bring home fruit. I usually wash it but that still does not guarantee no gnats. The best way to get rid of gnats is this. I get a quart bottle of cider vinegar. I put 2tbs of sugar, and 5 drops of dish detergent in the bottle. The detergent changes the viscosity of the mix so once they get in they can't get out. Put a piece of saran wrap on the top and hold it in place with a rubber band. Poke 3 or 4 holes in the top and leave it next to the source or close to the area that is infested with gnats. I thought these would be great as my wife hates the vinegar smell. But they do nothing. It's a great night light, but I have fairy lights for night lights. Don't waste your time or money on this product if you are trying to kill gnats. I don't know how this product works with mosquitoes, as I have no mosquito problem in the house.

They worked perfectly before and now I’m stuck with extra refills that don’t work. I’m now buying a generic version refill now that still has a clear background. They are cheaper and more importantly work like the original Zevos did. No longer killing bugs—I get a lot of flies—and not worth the cost. They used to be full by the start of the 3rd week. body: So I have mixed feelings on this… the good: crazy sticky adhesive area, soft and not blinding light, the adjustable plug that allows you to install it in outlets that run both horizontally and vertically, quick set up, and safe for my pets and kids with no harsh chemicals or zaps of electricity. I also really appreciate the additional pack of sticky pads that comes with it - there’s nothing worse than getting a great product that has a replaceable element and then discovering that you’ve got to shell out more money if you want to continue to use it down the road. The bad: it’s kind of a statement piece- it’s pretty big, and that mixed with the purple light does make it a bit of an eyesore and very noticeable as soon as you walk in the room. I’m also not sure how well the purple light works, because the 3 fruit flies who have decided to invade my kitchen still haven’t gotten themselves stuck to the pad yet. I was expecting it to work a little quicker and for the little buggers to be firmly attached to the sticky part by now, but I haven’t given up hope that one day soon I’ll be greeted by beautiful silence instead of a slight buzz when I walk into my kitchen.

title: Absolutely worth it. - EDIT: Reduced stars for low longevity
body: Edit: I'm still sold on the functionality of these things. The design is absolutely AWESOME! But the clear plastic ring that holds the LEDs gets cloudy and opaque after a while, and stops attracting the bugs. I'm super disappointed. I took one apart earlier today to see if there was anything I could do about it, but everything I did only made it worse. I might buy a 3D printer just so I can make some new ones because the design REALLY rocks on this thing when the LEDs aren't blocked by the bad choice in plastic. Side note: They're not really meant to be user serviceable, so I wouldn't expect anyone to be making replacement parts. If they could just make that white plastic ring out of something that doesn't get cloudy over time - I think they'd crush all their competition. Original review below for posterity. I got this and another of a different style at the same time. The other one is nowhere near as good as this. In just two days this thing caught all the stuff in the picture. I legit didn't even know I had full size goes flies in the house. The other style only had 2 fruit flies after 3 days. I highly recommend this style, as it's proved highly effective. After a week of temps in the mid 80s, we had a weather shift, dropping the overnight temps into the low 60s with very little wind. The next morning fruit does were everywhere, presumably drawn to the heat of the house. They were outside, inside, everywhere. We rent this cottage and the UV trap had already been use for two weeks before we arrived. There were a few random insects but nothing terribly impressive. When the fruit flies hit, I put out several traditional bait traps. The photos show the difference. At the time of the photos, the UV trap had been in steady operation for 3 weeks. The red/ fruit trap was only out for 2 hours!!! I'm not kidding and not exaggerating. This is two hours. There are two issues here. (1) Fruit flies don't seem particularly attracted to UV light and (2) the suction of the fan isn't remotely adequate.

title: Fabulous flying insect trapper!!
body: Living in the country, it’s inevitable that you will get a fly or two in the house with the doors opening and closing all of the time. Boy am I glad I did! I simply put the sticky pad in the quality built plug in, really easy to do, and the picture I posted was just from plugging it in last night! As you can see, it has attracted three flies I didn’t even know were in my house! title: Actually works!
body: To start off, I have purchased this item several times. My place started to have fruit flies especially during the summer. title: RECOMMEND!!! war on gnats story:
body: I have tried: Zevo Flying Insect Traps (RECOMMEND this product)Husaco Store 2 Flying Insect Traps & 2 Cartridges - Compatible with ZEVOM364A RefillKatchy Flying Insect Trap IndoorTerro Fruit Fly Traps - (RECOMMEND)I tried several products for my recent gnat/fruit fly/super tiny demons from hell infestation. I really wanted to like some, but basically overall the ZEVO was superior. Thankfully I bought that one initially, but did not realize how severe my infestation got (as I was away from home for abit). Zevo pretty immediately and quickly toned down the flying creatures, and I noticed quickly the trap filling up with more and more. A good week in it was basically all covered up.I ended up getting a total of 4 Zevo traps, in certain areas I knew would fly to at night. Night is very good at getting them. I think it helps having no other lights on  either. I will mention I also got Terro fly trap, and they are just lil tiny apple looking containers that you fill with some nasty vinegar mixture. I fill it up just a small amount, because honestly that is enough and I can keep refilling it. One I had to dump because of so many dead bodies and I refilled it up.I put one of those in my fridge just incase. And some near the other traps to try to attract them faster to the Zevo's light of death.The Katchy and offbrand zevo aka Husaco store traps, just basically didn't trap as many.... Like say a week went by and I could count the flies it was a handful. They just weren't as amazing/fast for me.I had such a drastic reduction with 2 Zevo's and now that I got 4 going, I think they might finally be eradicated. (With the Terro assists. I liked putting them by the sinks.---EDIT ---So. I was wrong. I noticed bugs before I went on another weekend trip and it was declining to a point I thought they were gone and with me being gone they were just able to breed more. This product still worked, But I needed more products for the war against the gnats.To start off. I have pets. And there is water bowl sources, litter boxes. etc.  I didn't seem to notice any issues or problems with the litter, thankfully did not need to make any changes there, maybe because I take care of it often enough.Products Used for the battle (Ill write recommended if I loved it) Over a course of 3 days I saw a drastic reduction and 4-5 days I'm having trouble finding any:More refill cartridges for this plug in -> Mistakenly thought the war ended, but these got full and I needed more.Dawn Platinum Powerwash Dish Spray, Dish Soap, Apple Scent, 16oz <- Recommended - good for dishes anyway. I sprayed inside the toilet after every flush. If they tried to breed in it, this stuff traps them and they cant fly or get out and they drown. This how you home make liquid traps, vinegar helps lure them to it. To be honest they didn't seem to care for the toilet, (which is kept shut). But I did this as precaution.Zevo Brand can spray - I stopped using because I needed alot, and it worked great kills on contact but gets used so fast, there is hardly enough in the can.  (Recommended Mighty spray below)  - also this is really expensive...Mighty Mint Peppermint Oil Insect Repellent Spray – Natural Indoor & Outdoor Bug Control for Spiders, Ants, Roaches, and More – Plant-Based, Extra-Strong Formula - 16 oz -> RECOMMENDED -> This has ALOT of spray. And it doesn't seem to kill IMMEDIATELY but wait 2-3 seconds and yeah, they stop moving. Unless you get a good clean direct close up shot. Was also nice, to spray them on the wall, they would immediately fall off.  PLUS you get to one on one gnats and take 'em down right where you see them.  I'd go around to windows and doors, and find them there. Pew, pew. Bit satisfying. And smell isn't so bad, but can be strong. In the heat of battle you might be overwhelmed. I'd take a break from the area, get a fan etc. Smell will dissipate eventually/gradually.Sticky traps, the yellow that has a tack and hangs from wall -40 Pack Fruit Fly Traps for Indoor, Fly Traps Outdoor, Sticky Fly Trap Strips Tape Killer Catcher Paper Ribbon, Flying Insect Trap for Bug, Gnat, Insect, Pest, Mosquito -> RECOMMENDED -> Good passive attack. These are useful in variety of spots. Gnats tend to scale the walls and go up to the ceiling where these bad boys come in handy.  I had one just in the wall not ceiling but high up so pets cant get to it. Was collecting quiet a few.TERRO Drain Insect Killer - T590 Drain Fly Killer Spray - Foam Treatment for Fruit Flies, House Flies, and CockroachesAlso Green Gobbler drain killer. -> (recommend)  I used the gobbler first, frankly I think both work and wil do the job. But this is a plus that it foams right up (not for long mind you) but  I did notice gnats gravitate towards it and immediately die.  What you need to do is use this stuff and then PLUG the holes. see below + more info.Aluvor Bathtub Stopper 2pcs Sink Stopper Tub Plug Bathroom Shower Drain Plug Silicone Bathtub Drain Plug Tub Drain Stopper Washbasin Stopper - RECOMMENDED - Now this is why I think I got away with one can of the foam. I didn't really need to reapply, but I did as precaution.  For sink, plug the tiny hole with tape, its a backup hole for overflow, most sinks should have it if not you are good. Then use the tiny one for the bathroom sink. And the other one for the tub. I closed off the sink and mostly used the bathroom sink as my main source for washing/cleaning things. I did notice a fly or two come out during this but they seem dazed and was easily able to hand kill them. I'd be ready to spray them down. After I was done and wasn't going to use a drain for awhile I'd foam it up again. So depending on this factor you might want more foam. (I didn't run out of the can yet, so can't say for sure). Either way if it is sealed up you have time to buy more if needed.No product found for kitchen sink drain blocker/stopper -> I had bought one but it didnt actually block. I ended up using a plastic throwaway cup and weighed it down with a can for good measure, pretty sure they don't have ant strength to come and go. And the other sink for disposal I had a sink stopper already which blocked that side completely. I sprayed the foam in both and tried to avoid using the sink.Wondercide - Fruit Fly Traps for Indoors - Fruit Fly Killer - Pet and People Safe - Made in USA & Plant Based - 5.4 oz - 2 Pack -> PLUS has a cover lid on top, pets might knock it over but can't step into it. I would see gnats crawling on top of it quite often. Just checked and imo these did as well as the raid one below. Double for less money I thought it was. And has a cover on it with holes for the bugs to go in.Raid Essentials Fruit Fly Trap for Indoors, Made with Essential Oils, Child and Pet Safe, 5.4 oz -> This worked it was catching ALOT. However my cat, stepped his back foot in it somehow, and it wasn't knocked over. I have no IDEA how this happened but I had to wash his leg off. This DID work well. You could see a layer of gnats forming on the top quickly.  - The expensiveness of this mixed with not being great around pets I can't recommend.I DO recommend those terro fruit fly traps that looks like red apples. Those are effective always have been. Thats my standard go to when I notice these usually from bananas. also not to expensive.Trash can with a LID -> I had ONE trash can with a LID so it was closed. I would use to throw stuff away in and took that outside often so they couldn't sneak in and have a party.  Hefty actually has one with a GOOD seal. However, I was unable to obtain the item as my local store had it in stock but it was damaged and had a hole on the side of the can.... So I settled for a regular lid that wasn't fully sealed but had a button to open it and I'd just close it after.  (Hefty Touch Lid  is the name). It was helpful for the cause. I think most have a trash can with a lid but if not it is highly RECOMMENDED.-- WHAT you need to check --Water sources, bowls etc. Pet bowls of water. pet FOUNTAINS. Need to be cleaned at least 1x every 24 hour period. Personally if I saw them sitting on anything I'd clean that immediately. I never saw them on the pet  fountain but when I  checked I saw so much in the filter it was gross. I didn't use the fountain at all until after I won the war. (Just too gross and I wouldn't feel comfortable using the same filter, so I opted to not use it at all).Look around for exploded water jugs you may have kept for emergencies. Those explode and leak all the time. Found out the hard way.After taking care of the drains and constant cleaning pet water sources, these guys disappeared. Finally.Bananas are no longer welcome.

title: Works - But Don't Expect Miracles
body: The principle of the Veyofly, utilizing a defined spectrum of light that flying insects are attracted to, assures that this device will reliably capture some flying pests.  Specifically, it seems most effective on small insects like gnats, fruit flies and mosquitos.  Whereas it is less effective attracting the common housefly.Although the Veyofly casts a bright circle (say, a bit larger than a foot in diameter) on the wall of a pleasing soft purple light, still it is no match for the bug attraction power of sunlight streaming indoors from your windows.  Specifically, in daylight, I've observed common house flies buzzing over and banging into the pane of a window that is immediately above where the Veyofly is illuminated.The problem is further compounded by the fact that house flies don't seem to be "night fliers".  For example, study what bugs swarm about over a porch light at night -- it's not black flies, but rather moths, mosquitos and tiny gnats.So, as your house becomes dark the "night flying bugs" will roam about and eventually be attracted to, and be caught, by the Veyofly.  Whereas, house flies that have parked themselves, at dusk, outside of the immediate glow of the Veyofly are much less likely to find the device, since, by my theory, they are not night fliers.However, the above aside, my two Veyoflys have indeed caught a few house flies.  But the kill rate, or effectiveness, seems like it's 10 to 1 in favor of the night fliers.  On balance, it should be noted that I do attempt to keep house flies out of the house in the first place, so my population of these pests may be low relative other bugs.Lastly, it is very important that a category of insects the Veyofly has success with are mosquitos.  For this reason alone it gets five stars.  Also, a big plus is having no stinking chemicals to deal with.  Changing out the Veyofly's "tacky card" every 2 - 3 weeks takes about 10 seconds, so maintenance is minimal.  OEM replacement tack cards on Amazon are a bit pricey, but generics at half the price are available -- no experience with the quality of the latter.

title: Best solution I've tried
body: I've been struggling with fungus gnats from my plants for months and I've tried everything. This is by far the best thing I've used. Every day, I see more gnats stuck to the card and I don't have to do anything except change the card when it gets full. It's not noisy like a zapper and the light isn't bothersome. It seems solidly built and the cost is extremely reasonable as well. I just bought more for my other rooms. Oh, and you can get refill cards as well.

title: You will NOT regret this purchase. Buy as many plug ins as you can afford!
body: light #1 out of 3. Plugged them in last night. They are all full less than 24hours later. I tried homemade traps. I tried everything. This trap is a life saver. No more drain flies coming for my laptop in the middle of the night. There are 2 different ways to use the traps. The second being covering a cup or water or wine. The cup of wine worked as well but the plug in lights are by far superior. I guess it really depends if the flys have a different source of water available. YOU WILL NOT REGRET THIS PURCHASE. I had to move the lights around to adjust. I found that a flat wall works best for the lights rather than a textured or tiled shiny wall. The light will shine better on regular drywall. 2 out of 3 of my plugs are plugged into a socket by the floor and they still work wonders. The other next to the sink where I believe they initially hatched their eggs in the drain. You should definitely keep one by the front door so any new flies coming in go right for the light before hatching eggs.

title: Tiny bug nightclub with a very strict no-exit policy
body: I used this to deal with a phorid fly / drain fly situation.It is not some instant bug apocalypse machine, but the sticky cards definitely showed that it was doing its job. There is also something weirdly satisfying about checking the card and seeing proof that the little freeloaders made poor life choices.Setup is simple. I like that it is quiet and does not involve spraying anything around the kitchen. The light doubles as a nice ambient night light for my kitchen. I did notice that it's most effective / catches the most flies overnight.One thing worth mentioning: this helps catch the adults, but you still need to deal with wherever they are coming from. I used it while also cleaning drains and trying to eliminate the source. The trap helped catch the stragglers and gave me a good visual of whether things were improving.Overall, it helped. Not magic, but effective enough that I would use it again if the tiny bug nightclub ever reopens.

title: Simple and somewhat effective
body: I think this is a great product, I feel like there should be more gnats that stick, as I see more swarming in my home, but maybe it just takes time.I don’t have another brand to compare this too, I see most people with zevo in their homes but was hoping for a cheaper alternative.It is pretty easy to setup just you might get a bit of the sticky glue on you but it comes off fine.You can see what it looks like at night, some gnats have been stuck already.

title: Works well for catching flies/nats
body: I think this product is good and works well for what you are paying for. It catches the flies and nats okay but over the coarse of two days has not caught as many as I think it could. It is easy to put together and very light weight. No scent to this product, in case your wondering if it smells. You can re-use this product for about a week before changing the filter. I am not a fan of how you can see the bugs being caught out in the open, especially since this is primarily used in the kitchen area (at least for me since that is where they hangout the most). Overall it does the job for what you pay for.

title: Not working
body: Reasonable price and easy to assemble, these did not attract a single fly in 24 hours. I'm not sure whether it is the Gizmo itself or the type of flies. The less expensive fly traps, vinegar and soap, and sticky traps also worked poorly. I put up pictures of the flies. The sticky trap pulled more flies than anything else, but this is a drop in the bucket. In the last two days, these flies have become ubiquitous. I have now tried five methods. I wish I knew what else to try. #UPDATE: What finally worked? Located a rotting onion beneath the rest of my veggies and tossed it. Bye bye flies.

title: Apple cider vinegar works better than this!
body: This doesn’t even deserve 1 star. It’s officially been 24hrs since it was delivered and plugged in. It has been in my kitchen, directly next to the fruit that sits on the counter. I currently have an INSANE amount of fruit flies due to “someone” leaving an opened applesauce in the pantry…. I did a test. I put a small medicine cap filled with apple cider vinegar and Dawn dish soap in a separate portion of my house, where I have seen the least activity of fruit flies. The kitchen area is over run with fruit flies. The photos speak for themselves. For fun, I even took a piece of cardboard and did a layer of Elmer school glue right after I plugged in the blue light. Again, the photos speak for themselves. You see how many fruit flies were trapped by the Elmers glue makeshift trap, in the short time it took to dry, compared to this $20 piece of junk. I truly don’t understand how this has so many great reviews. Photo 1 is the small cap filled with ACV and Dawn (the cloudiness are drowned fruit flies). Photo 2 is the school glue, photo 3 is this product 🙄🤨 I will be returning this!

title: After using since late last summer till now, Save your money and buy a bug/animal glue pad catcher
body: Purchased this over 6 months ago and have tried them in different rooms, areas, and heights, and I don't see them doing anything great. I had them in a spot for over a month and maybe one or two little noes see em bugs land on one by the door. Flies don't go on them I have watched them land or scurry right around it like it had no interest at all to them. Also, the way it is curved like a quarter moon is so close to the wall when you plug it in I don't think any bugs will go behind the cover then jump onto the pad. Most of the time there is never anything on them after a month even. It reminds me of those ways you catch a mouse glue pad type that is put in with a light. I am going to buy the mouse catch pads and put a night light by it. I think I will have better luck with that or a fly bug strip. And they don't last that long before you have to replace the pad and the price for the couple of replacements is way over priced.

title: It works… kind of
body: During the summer we occasionally have a fruit fly or two but never a huge issue until this year. Trying to find a solution that takes them completely out is hard to find so we started trying everything. We set out this light where they always hangout and after a couple weeks it’s only caught a maybe 10-15… not giving it one or two starts bc it’s done the job of attracting them and if you have a small issue but definitely recommend just doing dawn dish soap and apple cider vinegar in a shallow bowl is you have a major problem. The home remedy caught threes times as much as this trap.
